name: Upcoach
tagline: All-in-one platform for running group coaching programs: modules, client portals, habit tracking, session notes and action items.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The feature list looks intimidating but most of it is CRUD: programs, modules, lessons, client records, habit check-ins, session notes, action items. An agent can produce a working coach-and-client portal in a weekend, and if you coach five people it will be plenty. The gap is everything that touches other humans: payments, calendar booking, video calls, group chat, email reminders, and a client-facing experience that does not look like a hobby project. Your clients are the ones who have to log in, and they will judge the login page. Solo or small-cohort coaches can absolutely self-host this; anyone selling a premium program will feel the polish deficit fast.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted coach portal where you build a program of modules and lessons, enroll clients, and track their daily habit check-ins, session notes and action items in one place.
requirements: A host with a real domain and TLS, since clients log in from their own devices
Email sending for invites and reminders (Resend or Postmark API key)
Separate accounts for scheduling, payments and video if you want those
whatYouLose: Payments and subscription billing for your programs
Calendar booking and video call integration out of the box
Group chat, community feed and cohort engagement features
Mobile-friendly client experience that feels professional on day one
Someone else owning uptime, backups and client data security
moatNotes: The moat is not technical, it is that your paying clients see this thing. A half-built portal is a worse look than no portal.
whyPeopleStillPay: Coaches sell trust, and the tooling is part of the product they are selling. Upcoach bundles the parts that are individually easy but collectively annoying: onboarding flows, payment links, session scheduling, habit nudges, a client view that loads fast and looks paid-for. Once a cohort of thirty people is mid-program inside it, with history and check-in streaks and notes attached to each of them, migrating is a project nobody wants during a live cohort. The subscription is cheaper than the hours you would spend maintaining your own portal instead of coaching.
notes: Great fit for a solo coach with a handful of clients, bad fit the moment you need to charge money inside it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted group coaching portal. Single app, no SaaS dependencies except email sending.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), Prisma with SQLite, Tailwind, Auth.js with email magic links via Resend. Deploy target is a single Node process behind a reverse proxy.

Data model:
- User: email, name, role (COACH or CLIENT), createdAt
- Program: title, description, published flag
- Module: belongs to Program, title, order
- Lesson: belongs to Module, title, markdown body, order
- Enrollment: User + Program, startDate, status (ACTIVE, PAUSED, DONE)
- LessonProgress: Enrollment + Lesson, completedAt nullable
- Habit: belongs to Program, name, cadence (DAILY or WEEKLY)
- HabitCheckin: Enrollment + Habit, date, done boolean, note
- Session: Enrollment, scheduledAt, coachNotes markdown, clientVisibleSummary markdown
- ActionItem: Enrollment, text, dueDate, doneAt nullable, createdBy

Coach views: program builder with drag-to-reorder modules and lessons, client list with per-client detail page showing habit streaks, lesson progress, open action items, and a session notes timeline. One-click invite that emails a magic link.

Client views: dashboard with today's habit check-ins, next lesson, open action items, past session summaries. Lesson reader renders markdown and has a Mark complete button. Nothing else.

Explicitly out of scope: payments, calendar booking, video calls, group chat, notifications beyond invite and one daily check-in reminder cron, mobile apps, analytics, telemetry.

Secrets in .env: DATABASE_URL, AUTH_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, APP_URL. Ship a seed script with one coach, one 3-module program with two habits, and two demo clients with a week of check-in history. Include a README with setup, migrate, seed and deploy steps.
